form.label: DOC - Alert From BSL Lookups
form.description: DOC - guide for filtering non-baseline matches using Splunk lookup techniques

html.h1: Splunk Lookup Filtering Methods for Non-Matches
html.p: This dashboard provides various methods for filtering events that don't match your baseline lookup tables in Splunk.
When performing baseline analysis, you often need to identify events that are NOT in your baseline lookup table. These methods help you filter out baselined events to focus on potential anomalies.

panel.title: 🏆 Method 1: Using lookup and filtering for non-matches (RECOMMENDED)

pre.code: index=your_index sourcetype=your_sourcetype | lookup baseline_lookup.csv "process name" processport OUTPUT baselined | where isnull(baselined)

html.p: Best for: Most scenarios due to simplicity and performance

ul.li: Simple and clean syntax
Optimal performance
Easy to understand and maintain
Minimal resource usage
Direct filtering approach

panel.title: Method 2: Using subsearch with NOT IN for both fields

pre.code: index=your_index sourcetype=your_sourcetype | eval process_port_combo = 'process name' + ":" + processport | where NOT process_port_combo IN [ | inputlookup baseline_lookup.csv | eval process_port_combo = 'process name' + ":" + processport | return 1000 process_port_combo ]

html.p: Best for: Complex scenarios where you need to combine multiple fields for comparison

ul.li: You need to create composite keys from multiple fields
Complex field combinations are required
Advanced matching logic is needed

pre.code: index=your_index sourcetype=your_sourcetype | lookup baseline_lookup.csv "process name" processport OUTPUT baselined as is_baselined | where isnull(is_baselined) | fields - is_baselined

html.p: Best for: When you want to rename the output field for clarity and clean up the results

ul.li: Clear field naming with aliases
Explicit cleanup of temporary fields
Better documentation and readability

panel.title: Method 4: More explicit approach with join

pre.code: index=your_index sourcetype=your_sourcetype | join type=left "process name" processport [ | inputlookup baseline_lookup.csv | fields "process name" processport baselined ] | where isnull(baselined) | fields - baselined

html.p: Best for: When you need more control over the join operation or when working with complex lookup relationships

ul.li: Complex join logic is required
Multiple lookup tables need to be combined
Explicit control over join behavior is needed

html.p: Note: Less performant than Method 1, but more explicit

pre.code: index=your_index sourcetype=your_sourcetype | lookup baseline_lookup.csv "process name" processport OUTPUT baselined | eval status = if(isnull(baselined), "NOT_BASELINED", "BASELINED") | where status="NOT_BASELINED"

html.p: Best for: When you want to explicitly categorize and potentially analyze both baselined and non-baselined results

ul.li: Clear categorization of all events
Useful for comparative analysis
Easy to modify filters
Good for reporting and dashboards

html.p: Understanding the performance characteristics of each method helps you choose the right approach for your use case.
Best practices for implementing these lookup filtering methods in production environments.

ul.li: Keep lookup tables as small as possible
Use appropriate field types (string, number, boolean)
Regularly update and maintain lookup tables
Consider using automatic lookups for frequently used tables
Index key fields for better performance
Filter data as early as possible in the search pipeline
Use specific time ranges to limit data volume
Leverage summary indexing for frequently accessed baselines
Consider using acceleration for large lookup tables
Use the stats command instead of transaction when possible

pre.code: index=security earliest=-1h@h latest=@h sourcetype=windows:security | lookup baseline_processes.csv process_name OUTPUT is_baseline | where isnull(is_baseline) | stats count by process_name, dest

ul.li: Field Name Mismatches: Ensure field names in lookup match exactly (case-sensitive)
Data Type Issues: Convert fields to appropriate types before lookup
Large Lookup Tables: Consider using KV store or summary indexing
Memory Issues: Use subsearches carefully with large datasets

pre.code:
# Handle field name issues | eval process_name=lower('Process Name') | lookup baseline.csv process_name OUTPUT baselined
# Handle data type conversion | eval port_num=tonumber(port) | lookup baseline.csv process port_num OUTPUT baselined

html.p: Practical examples of using these methods in security monitoring scenarios.
Scenario: Detect non-baseline processes running on endpoints

pre.code: index=endpoint_data sourcetype=sysmon EventCode=1 | lookup approved_processes.csv Image OUTPUT approved | where isnull(approved) | stats count by Image, Computer | sort - count

index=network_data sourcetype=zeek:conn | lookup baseline_connections.csv id_orig_h id_resp_h id_resp_p OUTPUT baselined | where isnull(baselined) | stats count by id_orig_h, id_resp_h, id_resp_p | sort - count

html.p: Scenario: Identify unusual user login locations

pre.code: index=authentication sourcetype=windows:security EventCode=4624 | lookup user_normal_locations.csv user src_ip OUTPUT normal_location | where isnull(normal_location) | stats count by user, src_ip, dest | sort - count
index=dns_data sourcetype=zeek:dns | lookup approved_domains.csv query OUTPUT approved | where isnull(approved) | stats count by query, id_orig_h | sort - count

index=web_logs sourcetype=access_combined | lookup baseline_web_activity.csv clientip uri_path method OUTPUT normal_activity | where isnull(normal_activity) | stats count by clientip, uri_path, method, status | where count > 5
index=security_events | eval hour=strftime(_time, "%H") | lookup normal_activity_by_hour.csv user hour OUTPUT expected | where isnull(expected) | stats count by user, hour, activity
